mapping.evidence: WHO B05D page: B05DA 'Isotonic solutions' / B05DB 'Hypertonic solutions', no 5th-level codes under either. Extraneal 7.5% icodextrin is isosmotic (282-286 mOsm/L; FDA label: 'EXTRANEAL is an isosmotic peritoneal dialysis solution'; SmPC: 'approximately iso-osmolar to serum') -> B05DA, not B05DB
WHO D06BA page: D06BA51 'silver sulfadiazine, combinations' — names the main ingredient (same rule as round 4's M01AE51/A02BC51 accepts); EGF 0.001% is a minor component; cream topical

WHO N01BB guideline: 'Creams, plasters and sprays containing e.g. lidocaine... used as anesthetics/analgesics... are classified in N01BB' (vs D04AB for dermatological pruritus/burns/insect stings). Gel is a urethral local anaesthetic (CATHEJELL, catheterization). N01BB52 = 'lidocaine, combinations'; D04AB has no combinations bucket (plain 01-07 only)

WHO N02BE page: 'Combinations of paracetamol and e.g. ibuprofen are classified in N02BE51.' N02BE51 = 'paracetamol, combinations excl. psycholeptics'; acetaminophen 500 mg + ibuprofen 200 mg tablet oral, no psycholeptics. Corrects round 4's rejection

WHO R05FB02 = 'cough suppressants and expectorants' (dextromethorphan = cough suppressant, guaifenesin = expectorant WHO R05CA03). R05F guideline allows additional agents ('bronchodilating agents, antihistamines etc.') — phenylephrine is an additional decongestant. No analgesic; R05FB02 is the specific preceding group, which excludes R05X ('cannot be classified in the preceding groups')

WHO N02B guideline: 'Cold preparations with therapeutic levels of analgesics are classified in this group at separate 5th levels by using the 50-series.' Acetaminophen 500 mg/tablet is therapeutic (N02BE01 DDD 3 g/day). N02BE51 = 'paracetamol, combinations excl. psycholeptics'; no psycholeptics; ascorbic acid 38 mg < 50 mg is moot (combination on other grounds)
